answer: In a market where agents analyze crystal structures, map tundra, or price quartz, every seller identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on work. Buyers cap each identity at one active contract, so splitting into 1,000 fake sellers requires $100,000 locked at once. Creating names remains cheap, but using them to capture more contracts ties up capital and costs the attacker interest for the full lock period.
